title: The Miraculousness And Testimony Of The Quran 17th Degree Turning To The Quran And Referring To The Risale I Nur

questions.question: What did the traveller believe is the main purpose of life in this world?
questions.answer: Faith.

questions.question: What book did the traveller want to examine?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: Why did he want to look at the Qur’an?
questions.answer: He wanted to learn what it says.

questions.question: What did he say must be known first about the Qur’an?
questions.answer: That it comes from our Creator.

questions.question: Because he lived in the present age, what did he look at first?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What does the passage say the parts of the Risale-i Nur are made of?
questions.answer: Bright truths and strong explanations taken from the Qur’an.

questions.question: What kind of age does the passage describe?
questions.answer: A stubborn age with much disbelief.

questions.question: What happens to the Risale-i Nur in that difficult age?
questions.answer: People cannot defeat it.

questions.question: What does that show about the Qur’an?
questions.answer: That it is the source and authority behind it, and that it is from heaven, not from people.

questions.question: What do the two named sections in the Risale-i Nur show about the Qur’an?
questions.answer: They show many ways the Qur’an is miraculous.

questions.question: How do people respond when they truly see that proof?
questions.answer: They admire it and praise it.

questions.question: Did the traveller try to explain every proof there?
questions.answer: No. He left that to the Risale-i Nur and only gave a short mention of a few points.

questions.question: How is the traveller described at the start of the passage?
questions.answer: He is hard-working, never satisfied, and always searching.

questions.question: What two things did he connect with faith?
questions.answer: The goal of life and what life really is.

questions.question: Who did he speak to before beginning his search?
questions.answer: His own heart.

questions.question: How is the Qur’an described in the passage?
questions.answer: As a very famous, shining, and wise book.

questions.question: What does the Qur’an do in every age?
questions.answer: It challenges those who refuse to accept it.

questions.question: What did the traveller begin to do after saying he must first prove where the book came from?
questions.answer: He started searching.

questions.question: What did he examine first before speaking more about the Qur’an?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: From where does the Risale-i Nur get its light and teachings?
questions.answer: From the Qur’an.

questions.question: What does the passage say no one can do to the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: No one can overcome it.

questions.question: What does that teach about the Qur’an’s speech?
questions.answer: It is from Allah above, not made by humans.

questions.question: Which writings are named as giving one proof with many sides of the Qur’an’s wonder?
questions.answer: The Twenty-Fifth Word and the end of the Nineteenth Letter.

questions.question: After seeing those proofs, what simple path did the traveller choose?
questions.answer: He chose to mention only a few signs of the Qur’an’s greatness.

questions.question: What truth about life had the traveller already learned?
questions.answer: That faith is the aim and true life of a person.

questions.question: Which book did he call the one spoken by the Being he was seeking?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: What did he want to find out from that book?
questions.answer: What it says.

questions.question: Before listening to the Qur’an’s message, what did he think needed to be settled?
questions.answer: Whether it really came from the Creator.

questions.question: Why did he turn first to the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: Because he was living in this time.

questions.question: How are the many parts of the Risale-i Nur explained in the passage?
questions.answer: As shining points and solid explanations taken from the Qur’an.

questions.question: In what way is the Risale-i Nur working?
questions.answer: It is bravely spreading the truths of the Qur’an everywhere.

questions.question: What makes its success important in an age of disbelief?
questions.answer: It shows its support comes from the Qur’an.

questions.question: What is the result when someone sees the proof mentioned from those two sections?
questions.answer: The person stops objecting and feels respect for the proof.

questions.question: Did the traveller deny that there are many proofs?
questions.answer: No. He said there are many, and he would only point to a few.

questions.question: What does this tell us about the traveller’s method of study?
questions.answer: He wanted to be careful and make sure the foundation was true first.

questions.question: What was the traveller searching for through the Qur’an?
questions.answer: The word of the One he was seeking.

questions.question: What three praising ideas are said about the Qur’an near the start?
questions.answer: It is very well-known, very bright, and very wise.

questions.question: Who is invited by the Qur’an’s challenge in every age?
questions.answer: People who refuse to submit to it.

questions.question: What was the first thing the traveller said must be shown?
questions.answer: That the Qur’an is from the Creator.

questions.question: What work did he use first in his search?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: What is said about the contents of its many parts?
questions.answer: They come from the Qur’an and explain it well.

questions.question: What kind of spirit does the passage give to the Risale-i Nur’s work?
questions.answer: Brave and active.

questions.question: Why is it meaningful that nobody defeats it in this age?
questions.answer: Because that points to the strength of the Qur’an behind it.

questions.question: Is the Qur’an described as man-made or sent from above?
questions.answer: Sent from above.

questions.question: What do the proof sections named in the passage help show?
questions.answer: They help show many signs of the Qur’an’s miraculous nature.

questions.question: When a person understands that proof, how does the person react?
questions.answer: With admiration instead of criticism.

questions.question: What did the traveller decide to do instead of giving all the proofs himself?
questions.answer: He let the Risale-i Nur handle that and gave only a short reminder of a few points.

questions.question: What did the traveller say life is truly about?
questions.answer: Having faith.

questions.question: To what part of himself did he speak?
questions.answer: His heart.

questions.question: Which book did he choose to study?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: What claim about the Qur’an did he want to test first?
questions.answer: That it is from the Creator.

questions.question: What did he do because he lived in today’s time?
questions.answer: He first looked at the Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: According to the passage, what is the Risale-i Nur built from?
questions.answer: Clear lights and explanations from the Qur’an.

questions.question: What is the Risale-i Nur trying to spread?
questions.answer: The truths of the Qur’an.

questions.question: In what kind of time is it doing this work?
questions.answer: In a difficult time full of stubborn unbelief.

questions.question: What fact about the Risale-i Nur is used as evidence in the passage?
questions.answer: That no one can beat it.

questions.question: What conclusion is drawn from that fact?
questions.answer: The Qur’an is its true source and is not human speech.

questions.question: Which two writings are named for giving a strong proof of the Qur’an’s wonder?
questions.answer: The Twenty-Fifth Word and the end of the Nineteenth Letter.

questions.question: What did the traveller choose to do after mentioning those writings?
questions.answer: He chose to point only briefly to some of the Qur’an’s greatness.

questions.question: What kind of learner does the traveller seem to be from this passage?
questions.answer: A serious learner who keeps searching for truth.

questions.question: What did he say is both the goal of life and the real meaning of life?
questions.answer: Faith.

questions.question: What holy book did he plan to examine?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: What made the Qur’an special in his words?
questions.answer: It is widely known, full of light, and full of wisdom.

questions.question: What does the Qur’an do to people who do not accept it?
questions.answer: It calls them to answer its challenge.

questions.question: Before studying its message, what question did the traveller want answered?
questions.answer: Whether the Qur’an truly came from Allah.

questions.question: What book did he use first to help with that question?
questions.answer: The Risale-i Nur.

questions.question: How does the passage connect the Risale-i Nur to the Qur’an?
questions.answer: It says the Risale-i Nur takes its truths from the Qur’an.

questions.question: What is important about the Risale-i Nur’s strength in this age?
questions.answer: No one can defeat it even in a time of disbelief.

questions.question: What does that strength point to about the Qur’an?
questions.answer: That it is the heavenly source behind it.

questions.question: What is shown by the proof in the two named parts of the Risale-i Nur?
questions.answer: Many signs that the Qur’an is miraculous.

questions.question: What feeling replaces objections when someone understands that proof?
questions.answer: Respect and praise.
